title: The Necessary Weather
premise: Zephyrine Okonkwo, a celebrated restaurant critic who lost her sense of taste after her mother's death, has built a career on evocative prose for flavors she cannot feel. When a box of undelivered letters surfaces behind a wardrobe in her late mother's house — letters Zephyrine wrote and never sent during the estrangement — she must return to Lagos before the house sale closes to confront what she abandoned. There, among her mother's old market friends and a half-sister she never knew existed, she discovers the letters were found years ago and answered; her mother's replies sit unanswered in the same box. Relearning taste through her mother's pepper soup recipe, Zephyrine finally sends a letter of her own — to herself, forgiving the girl who left — and chooses to stay through one full rainy season before deciding who she will be.
about_author: Juniper Vane is the pen name of a former food writer who spent a decade covering West African diaspora kitchens before turning to fiction. She lives between two cities and writes at the hour when the light makes both look like home.

chapters.title: The Vocabulary of Almost
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. At a tasting menu in London, she writes a rave review of a dish she cannot taste, then learns the house in Lagos is being sold in six weeks. The chapter establishes her polished fraudulence and grief. Emotional beat: the quiet panic of a life built on borrowed language.

chapters.title: What the Wardrobe Kept
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Packing up the family home via video call with the estate agent, she spots the box behind the wardrobe: forty-one unsent letters from her twenties, and beneath them, replies in her mother's hand that she never received. Emotional beat: vertigo — the past was not silent after all.

chapters.title: Harmattan Season
chapters.summary: Zephyrine arrives in Lagos against her editor's advice. The city assaults her with smells she can register but not savor. She meets Auntie Bisi, her mother's oldest friend, who recognizes her instantly and says nothing kind. Emotional beat: homesickness for a place that remembers you better than you remember it.

chapters.title: The Other Daughter
chapters.summary: Alternating POV with Adaeze, the half-sister raised in the house, now overseeing its sale. Their first meeting is transactional and barbed; Adaeze resents the famous sister who appears only to sign papers. Emotional beat: rivalry as a mask for identical abandonment.

chapters.title: Letters, Answered
chapters.summary: Zephyrine reads her mother's replies chronologically: anger, then worry, then a final letter asking only that Zephyrine cook one meal in the kitchen before leaving. She learns her mother died knowing she'd come back someday. Emotional beat: grief reorganized into shame, then tenderness.

chapters.title: Market Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Auntie Bisi drags Zephyrine to Balogun Market to buy ingredients, forcing her to bargain, taste-test, and fail publicly. A vendor's scolding awakens a flicker of sensation — heat, salt, something. Emotional beat: humiliation as the first door back into the body.

chapters.title: The Recipe Is a Argument
chapters.summary: Adaeze reveals their mother changed the family pepper soup recipe after Zephyrine left — added bitterleaf, 'for the ones who go.' The sisters fight over whose version is true. Rising tension: the sale deadline looms and a developer offers cash for a fast close. Emotional beat: inheritance contested as love contested.

chapters.title: One Meal in the Kitchen
chapters.summary: Climax. On the last night before closing, Zephyrine cooks her mother's final version alone, hands shaking, following letters instead of memory. Midway, taste returns — violently, painfully — and she weeps into the pot. Adaeze comes down and eats with her in silence. Emotional beat: the price of survival paid back in full.

chapters.title: Closing
chapters.summary: Zephyrine signs the sale papers but keeps the wardrobe, shipping it to her flat. She writes a new letter — to the girl who left — and mails it to her own address. Adaeze agrees to visit; Auntie Bisi gives her a jar of ground crayfish 'for the road.' Emotional beat: release without erasure.

chapters.title: The Necessary Weather
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV, months later. Her review column changes: honest about what she cannot know, praised for it. In London, rain on the window tastes faintly of pepper soup. She begins a novel about two sisters and a kitchen. Emotional beat: belonging rebuilt as practice, not place — weather you choose to stand in.
